input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper clears and reuses a single shared statistics dict for every call. Concurrent coroutines running the same decorated function overwrite each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather over several calls of the same @retry-decorated coroutine function. Each call starts with stats.clear() and then writes into the same dict. Impact: the statistics mix across the calls and are wrong. The previous per-call copy.statistics kept them separate.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is shared, cleared and reused on every call, so concurrent coroutines overwrite each other's stats. It covers the async-gather trigger the label names, and it contrasts this with the previous per-call copy.
